behaviour_changes: Chart history is the server window only: candleBatch {replace:true} REPLACES the local series (no merge with sessionStorage, resume snapshot or finalBattleSnapshot candles). Two devices connecting at different times render identical bars.

The line-chart store is one continuous 1 bar/second series across rounds and cooldown (flat candles with battle_id null accepted); it is never reset at battleEnd / newBattleStarted / battleSnapshot id switch / cooldownEnded. Cap raised from 300 to 900 candles.
No vertical cliff on sign-in/resume: the series is setData from the server batch (active round included); a store batch generation change is the only trigger for setData besides tab-visible resume.

Viewport is fixed (barSpacing = plotWidth/80, rightOffset 18) on create/resize; no setVisibleRange over N bars, no re-zoom at round boundaries, no manual price-scale mode. Pan/pinch still glides back after 2 s idle.

Time cursor (.chart-expiry-line/.chart-expiry-tag) is always mounted; x = pixel of newest bar + (serverNow - barStart) x live bar spacing, serverNow from an EMA of server_time. It keeps gliding through the cooldown because flat candles keep arriving; hidden (class) only until the series has data.
ROUND ENTRY line can no longer leave the visible price range (AreaSeries autoscaleInfoProvider widens the range to include it; price scale always autoscaled).

Volume histogram uses a fixed 0..max(volume over the whole loaded series) scale, so a $100k bar is always taller than a $10k bar and heights match across devices; the in-progress bar's volume now grows live from priceUpdate.volume.

Closed bars carry the exact server close (late closes applied with historicalUpdate or a store re-apply); only the in-progress bar is eased. RAF stops the price easing when converged and runs glow/cursor at ~30 fps; series.update only when the value changed; no per-frame getBoundingClientRect.

notes_for_pdf:
**What was wrong.** The trading chart assembled its history from four different, device-specific sources: the server's `candleBatch` (which only contained the last three *completed* rounds, never the active one), whatever live ticks this device happened to receive, a per-tab `sessionStorage` mirror of closed candles, and a "resume snapshot" written by `ResumeSyncBridge`. Every one of those was merged into `lineChartStore` and then trimmed to 200–300 points. The result was that a phone signing in mid-round drew a single vertical segment from an hours-old close to the live price (the "cliff"), and two devices that connected at different times held different bar sets, so the charts never matched. On top of that, `NewChart.jsx` tore the series down at every round boundary (the store was reset at `battleEnd` and `newBattleStarted`) and re-zoomed with `setVisibleRange` over however many bars existed — with one bar that collapsed the zoom (giant bars, newest bar at 25 % of the plot), which is the "time line jumps far left, then moves right when the next round starts" symptom. The time cursor was driven by a hand-built map that read `timeScale().options().barSpacing`, a value lightweight-charts never updates (always the default 6 px), and by the phone's own clock, so it sawtoothed and stalled. The ROUND ENTRY line was a native price line, which lightweight-charts excludes from autoscale, so after ~60 s it scrolled off the axis. The volume histogram autoscaled to the visible window and the in-progress bar had no volume, so a $10k bar could look as tall as an earlier $100k bar. Finally the RAF loop called `series.update` and two `getBoundingClientRect()` reads every frame forever.

**What changed (frontend, `/home/claude/wb/frontend`).** Contract C1 makes the server the single source: the `/line-chart` gateway now publishes one continuous 1-second candle stream that spans rounds *and* the cooldown (flat candles when nothing traded), sends the last 600 seconds plus the in-progress bucket as `candleBatch { replace: true }` on connection, and adds `bucket_ts` + `volume` to `priceUpdate`.

- `src/stores/lineChartStore.js` is now that stream: one array, deduped by bucket second, capped at 900 (15 min). `replaceCandles` drops everything local on a batch; `appendClosedCandle` appends the exact server close; `upsertInProgress` only moves the newest bar's value and volume. `resetLineChart()` deliberately keeps the candles — the battle transition helpers still call it, but a new round no longer wipes the chart.
- `src/utils/useWebSocket.js` (line-chart handlers only): no `subscribe` on connect (the server emits the batch itself), `subscribe { reason: 'resync' }` on foreground/stale, `candleClosed` accepted for every second including `battle_id: null` cooldown candles, `server_time` fed into a server-clock estimate (`src/live/services/chartClockService.js`), `priceUpdate` forwarded with `bucket_ts`/`volume`. Battle transitions no longer unsubscribe/resubscribe the room (that 60–100 ms gap lost a candle per device).
- `src/components/NewChart.jsx`: `setData` only when the store's batch generation changes or the tab becomes visible again, `update` otherwise. The viewport is fixed once (`barSpacing = plotWidth / 80`, `rightOffset 18`) on create and resize — never re-zoomed. The cursor is a real wall-clock cursor: `x = timeToCoordinate(newestBar) + frac × liveBarSpacing`, where `frac = clamp((serverNow − barStart)/1000, 0, 1.25)` and the live spacing comes from `logicalToCoordinate(i+1) − logicalToCoordinate(i)`. Because flat candles keep arriving during the cooldown, the cursor stays where the round ended and glides right, exactly like the bars around it. It is always mounted; a class hides it only until the first bar exists. The AreaSeries gets an `autoscaleInfoProvider` that widens the range to include the entry price (manual price-scale mode is gone), and the histogram gets a fixed `0..max(volume over the whole loaded series)` scale. Closed bars are written with the exact server close (late closes via `update(bar, true)`); only the in-progress bar is eased; the loop drops to ~30 fps once converged; plot offsets are measured on resize only. Pure helpers live in `src/live/services/chartGeometryService.js`.
- Removed: the `sessionStorage` candle mirror (`persistCandleClosedSession.js` is now an inert shim), resume-snapshot candles (`hydrateMatchFromResume.js`, `ResumeSyncBridge.jsx` chart subscriber, `Matches.jsx` re-hydration), `finalBattleSnapshot.candles`, and the dead `chartStreamService.js`.

**Why it is safe.** No money math is touched; the chart is display-only and every path that mutates it is covered by 28 `node --test` specs (`node --test "src/**/*.test.js"`): dedupe/replace/in-progress precedence, flat cooldown candles, late closes, the 900 cap, whole-series max volume, the fixed viewport, the cursor hand-off across an append, ROUND ENTRY range widening and the histogram scale. A legacy server batch without `replace: true` still merges, and a `priceUpdate` without `bucket_ts` falls back to the tick's own second, so the client also runs against the old backend. `npx vite build` is clean and lint is at or below the previous baseline for every touched file (the repo's `eslint.config.js` needs the one-line fix listed in the requests to run under ESLint 10 at all).

**How to test.** After the stack restart: sign in on a phone mid-round — the chart must show the current round from its start with no vertical segment; open a desktop tab at a different time and compare (`tools/chart-parity-capture.cjs`) — same bars; watch a round end (`tools/round-boundary-shots.cjs`): the dashed time line stays at the end of the round and keeps moving right through the cooldown with no jump to the left and no zoom change; let the price trend away from ROUND ENTRY — the purple line must stay on screen; place a $100k order then a $10k order — the second bar must be visibly shorter. DevTools Performance: with no ticks the chart pane should not repaint at 60 fps.
